title: Corrective Action Plan for Program Integrity Update
supports: Minnesota submitted a revised program-integrity CAP in response to CMS Administrator Oz's January 6, 2026 letter.
DHS said notices of revalidation requirements were sent to all 5,640 providers in the then-defined high-risk service categories between January 23 and January 28, 2026.
DHS planned high-risk revalidation to include in-person/unannounced site visits, fingerprint background studies for controlling-interest individuals, and verification of provider credentials.
DHS set an April 1, 2026 application deadline and May 31, 2026 target to complete revalidation and deactivate noncompliant providers.

DHS described an enhanced prepayment-review project in which Optum would flag potentially concerning fee-for-service claims each payment cycle, while unflagged claims could be released and flagged claims routed for policy/program review and possible OIG investigation.

DHS stated it paused payments for 14 high-risk services on December 23, 2025 for enhanced prepayment review; in the first cycle roughly 1,700 claims were flagged and 14 were denied after DHS review/policy consultation, while the others were released.

does_not_support: A revalidation notice or disenrollment is not proof of fraud.
A claim flagged by Optum is not necessarily fraudulent or ultimately denied.
The 5,640 figure was a plan-stage provider universe and should not be confused with later revalidation outcome counts.
This state CAP is Minnesota's proposed/committed response; CMS's assessment of adequacy is a separate federal source.
